quiz.title: Integration Exercise 7.1 Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on the standard integrals from Exercise 7.1 — powers, sin/cos, sec², e^x and 1/x. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score. Add + C to every antiderivative.
quiz.about: Integration as the inverse of differentiation; standard integrals by inspection

questions.explanation: Use the power rule ∫ xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n+1) + C. With n = 3 you get x⁴/4 + C. Check by differentiating: d/dx(x⁴/4) = x³.
Integration reverses differentiation. Since d/dx(sin x) = cos x, the antiderivative of cos x is sin x + C.
d/dx(tan x) = sec² x, so ∫ sec² x dx = tan x + C.
The power rule fails when n = −1. Instead ∫ (1/x) dx = ln|x| + C, because d/dx(ln x) = 1/x.
The exponential function is its own derivative, so it is also its own integral: ∫ e^x dx = e^x + C.
Since d/dx(−cos x) = sin x, the antiderivative of sin x is −cos x + C. Watch the sign — it is the common slip here.
Integrate term by term: ∫ 3x² dx = x³ and ∫ 2 dx = 2x. Together, x³ + 2x + C.
A constant k integrates to kx + C, since d/dx(kx) = k. So ∫ 5 dx = 5x + C.

faq.q: What does Exercise 7.1 of Class 12 Maths cover?
faq.a: It introduces integration as the inverse process of differentiation and asks you to find the antiderivatives of standard functions — powers of x, sin and cos, sec², e^x and 1/x — mostly by inspection. It is the foundation the rest of the chapter builds on.

faq.q: Why must I always add + C to an indefinite integral?
faq.a: Any two antiderivatives of the same function differ only by a constant, because the derivative of a constant is zero. The + C (the constant of integration) represents that whole family of curves. An answer without it is marked incomplete.

faq.q: Why is the integral of 1/x written as ln|x| and not just ln x?
faq.a: The power rule xⁿ⁺¹/(n+1) breaks down when n = −1. The correct antiderivative is ln|x| + C; the absolute value keeps it valid for negative x as well, where ln x alone is undefined.

faq.q: How do I check whether my integration answer is right?
faq.a: Differentiate your result. If it gives back the original integrand, the answer is correct. This reverse-check works for every question in Exercise 7.1 and is worth doing under exam pressure.
